title: Serially trained associative memories cause catastrophic forgetting in pathway models

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Serially trained associative memories cause catastrophic forgetting in pathway models

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When two associative memories are trained one after another in ODE pathway models, all biological and random models show catastrophic forgetting in which both memories are lost, whereas two UCS-based memories can be stored serially or in parallel.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.5. Can Networks Be Trained to Keep More Than One Memory?

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: When more complex memories were tested, here AM-AM memory pairs, when created serially all biological and random models showed catastrophic forgetting wherein both are lost.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.5. Can Networks Be Trained to Keep More Than One Memory?”. Scope: 35 BioModels pathway models and 35 size-matched random gene-circuit models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-12: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.89

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The universal statement over a finite model set is especially discriminating and readily falsified by one counterexample. Published protocols and public biological models support replication.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply serial and parallel two-memory protocols to all eligible biological and matched random models, then score retention of zero, one, or both memories. Any serial AM-AM case retaining a memory refutes the universal forgetting statement.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Random models must be regenerated consistently.

Eligibility constraints reduce the tested memory-pair set.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.94
operationalizability: 0.97
data existence: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.84
analysis feasibility: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Serial versus parallel training and the four pair types are specified, and the repository implements two-memory tests for biological and size-matched random models. Re-running those pairings decides whether associative pairs are uniformly lost while UCS pairs are not. The result is a property of this protocol, which is exactly the claim's scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Train two associative memories in series, and separately two UCS-based memories in series and in parallel, on the biological models and the size-matched random models. Loss of both associative memories in every model, together with retention of paired UCS memories, would confirm the claim; retention of serial associative pairs, or failure of serial UCS pairs, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Catastrophic forgetting is scored only for node triples that already passed the single-memory screen, so the denominator is selected.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.76
analysis feasibility: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.8
